wikitext: This is our top-level category; looking at it another way, it is the root category. wikitext:
'''For a full list of help pages, see [[Help:Contents]],''' which includes non-local help pages and is automatically transcluded from [[w:c:help|Wikia Help]].


===About this category===
This category is intended to contain all the '''local''' "help" pages for this Wikia: pages that can help contributors and/or readers. If you find helpful pages that you think should be here, you may include them here just by typing <nowiki>[[Category:Help]]</nowiki> on them.

Most, but not all, have "Help:" at the beginning of their page names and are therefore in the "Help" namespace; an automatically-generated list of those can be found at [[Special:AllPages]] by running down the "Namespace" menu.


===Getting more help===
You can also:
* Ask questions at our local [[Blog:Recent posts|Blogs]].
* Talk to one of the [[Special:ListUsers/sysop|site administrators]] or any currently active contributor (the people whose names appear on [[Special:RecentChanges|the "Recent changes" page]]); use their user talk pages.
* If you can't find what you need on this wiki, you can seek help at the [[w:|Central Wikia]], especially at the [[w:Forum:Index|Central forum]].

If you still need help, you may want to contact the [[w:Community Team|Wikia Community Team]].
[[Category:Browse]]

title: Category:Greece
wikitext:
'''Greece''' is one of the countries that was chosen for missions by Dante's team due to Greece's great historical and cultural territory. Many of the Greco-Roman legends and mythologies were inspired by the Titans and so was visited by the [[Huntik Foundation]] for a number of missions including the secret of [[Madea Island]], the [[Temple of Poseidon]], and the recovery of the [[Titan]], [[Medusa]].

title: Category:Merchandise
wikitext:
{{Media}}[[File:Merchandise.png|200px|thumb|A display table of ''Huntik'' merchandise]]
The '''Huntik Merchandise''' are collectible items that fans can buy to show their support for the show. In addition to the ''[[Huntik Trading Card Game]]'', the merchandise for Season 1 includes a collection of miniature figures and Amulets released by [[Tridimensional]], and a range of 6" action figures released by [[Upper Deck]]. In 2010, a mobile app, [[Huntik: Titan Defence]], was released alongside numerous DVDs. 

Coinciding with the release of Season 2 in 2011, the merchandise was produced by the Italian toy company, [[Giochi Preziosi]], who released 30 new miniature figures, 3 6" action figures, 4 Amulet Launcher figures amongst numerous other products notably the roleplay [[Willblade]].

title: Category:Rollback
wikitext:
Rollback means that the user may revert edits not just to the previous version but to the version of the previous editor, in one click, in the case that a vandal attempts to edit and vandalize a page through multiple edits.

Users with Rollback ability by default includes all Bureaucrats and Administrators. Rollback may be granted to non-administrators as well as added protection against vandalism.

'''Mission/Feature cards'''  consist of [[:Category:Mission cards|Missions]] and [[:Category:Feature cards|Features]]. title: Category:Destroyed Titans
wikitext:
[[Category:Titans]]
'''Destroyed Titans''' are [[Titans]] that have been entirely erased through the use of dark magic or whose physical form has been destroyed due to the destruction of their [[Amulet]]. While a Titan's spirit is usually immortal and returns safely to its Amulet when a standard battle is lost, there are rare instances where a Titan is permanently lost to its Seeker and can no longer be summoned. In some cases, the spiritual energy of a Titan lives on and is permanently returned to the [[Spirit World]], while in other cases, the Titan entirely ceases to exist and is considered deceased.

title: Category:Gaia-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Gaia.png|thumb|100px]]
'''Gaia-Titans''' are a type of [[Titan]] which tend to be protective and helpful. Gaia-Titans are strongly tied to nature, particularly wood or plants. Because of these ties, most of them are green or greenish-brown. Some may be covered in bark or leaves, with some even looking like walking trees, such as [[Dark Dryad]]. ''Gaia'' means Earth in Greek, so these Titans are essentially ''Earth-Titans'' or ''Nature-Titans''. Gaia-Titan amulets tend to be a pale silver white with a light green gem. A notable exception is the [[Amulet of Will]] for [[Overlos]]. Many Gaia Titans are found mainly in Ireland.

title: Category:Draco-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Draco.png|right|100px]]
'''Draco-Titans''' are a type of [[Titan]] featured prominently in European legends, particularly those of Medieval England. The fighting style and noble, chivalrous nature that most of them possess, inspired people to act the same and developed into the code of chivalry followed by knights. Draco-Titans' amulets are usually steel-blue with a grayish-pink gem in the center.

title: Category:Hecto-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Hecto Titans.png|thumb|100px]]
'''Hecto-Titans''' are [[Titans]] based upon Egyptian legends. Many Hecto-Titans appear like mummies with a monstrous appearance, earning them a place as the monsters residing in Egyptian tombs. Their terrible nature and taking enjoyment from chaos and destruction means that bonding [[Seekers]] need to possess a similar attitude. Their amulets tend to be yellow with blue and green highlights and a pale silver gem in the center.

title: Category:Legendary Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}
The '''Legendary Titans''' are an incredibly rare, powerful type of [[Titan]] which were originally controlled by [[Lord Casterwill]] and his [[Casterwill family|family]] and whose [[Rings]] and [[Amulets]] were later hidden with greater safeguards than the Amulets of any other Titans. The Legendary Titans find their places in the legends of many ancient civilizations and were sometimes considered gods. If a Seeker attempts to use a Legendary Titan without the [[Amulet of Will]] or without passing the proper Casterwill test, they may be put under a powerful [[Curse of the Legendary Titans|curse]]. Three Legendary Titans, [[Tao]], [[Behemoth]], and [[Araknos]], are involved in a ritual to summon [[Overlos]] from the [[Amulet of Will]].

title: Category:Meso-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Meso.png|thumb|100px]]
'''Meso-Titans''' are powerful [[Titans]] that are difficult to control. They tend to be aggressive and may cause collateral damage if not watched carefully. Some Meso-Titans control powerful natural forces, such as earthquakes, hurricanes, and tornadoes. Others use combat attacks based on stomping, jumping, and spinning. Meso-Titans often resemble creatures of Native American and Central American stories, such as fierce warriors and totem like monsters. Mesosphere is the middle part of the Earth's atmosphere. Only a [[Seekers|Seeker]] with a very strong will can bond with, let alone control, a Meso-Titan. Meso-Titan Amulets are typically grey with black or yellow highlights and a blue gem.
[[Category:Titans by type]]

title: Category:Litho-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Litho.png|thumb|100px]]'''Litho-Titans''' are a very durable type of [[Titan]] because most of them are composed of rocks or ice. Litho-Titans usually carve themselves a place in history, even among humans who know nothing about [[Seekers]] or magic. [[Metagolem]] became the famous Golem of Prague. [[Gar-Ghoul]] inspired the gargoyle statues on the rooftops across Europe. [[Fenris]] and [[Ymir]] are famous among Norse mythology, being responsible for the birth and death of the world. Litho-Titans act almost as if they want to be known for their power. Lithosphere is the ground part of Earth. Litho-Titan [[Amulets]] tend to be stone grey, with occasional light blue highlights for ice-based Titans, and have a purple gem in the center with yellow outline around the gem.

title: Category:Krono-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Krono.png|100px|thumb]]
'''Krono-Titans''' are [[Titans]] that are based off of Greek or Roman mythology. These Titans tend to be warriors, a fitting position considering the war-like nature of the Greeks during ancient history. The word 'Krono-Titan' may be based on [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cronus Kronos] of mythology, the imprisoned Greek Titan and father of Zeus. Krono-Titan Amulets tend to be orange and yellow with an aqua gem.

title: Category:Yama-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Yama Titans.png|100px|thumb]]
'''Yama-Titans''' are clever and often overly independent. They often think that their way of doing something is better than their bonded [[Seekers|Seeker]]; because of this, successfully controlling a Yama-Titan can require concentrating exactly on what one wants them to do. Human-like Yama-Titans often have features common to Asian myths, such as clothing or weaponry. Yama-Titans were appropriately common in ancient Asia. People told stories about them, and these stories eventually became myths. Yama-Titan amulets tend to be dark green with black, navy or silver highlights with a pale green gem. A notable exception is the [[ring]] of the Legendary Titan [[Tao]].

title: Category:Swara-Titans
wikitext:
{{Type}}[[File:Swara Titans.png|100px|thumb]]
'''Swara-Titans''' are a type of [[Titan]], most often used by villains, and are based upon African legends and insects. Like [[Araknos]], a large number of Swara-Titans tend to lean toward arthropods such as arachnids and insects. Swara-Titan [[Amulets]] tend to be brown with a darker brown or gold trim and a red gem.

title: Category:Huntik Foundation Missions
wikitext:
'''Huntik Foundation missions''' are assigned to [[Huntik Foundation]] teams by the [[Huntik Foundation Council]]. These missions involve uncovering more information regarding [[magic]] and [[Titans]] as well as preventing [[the Organization]] from achieving their nefarious goals. Many notable missions were assigned by [[Guggenheim]] to the team of [[Dante Vale]], [[Sophie Casterwill]], [[Lok Lambert]], [[Zhalia Moon]], and newcomer [[Den Fears]]. For a chronological list of missions, see [[List of Huntik Foundation Missions]]. 
[[Category:Huntik Foundation]]
